utility.notes: DTE Energy is Ann Arbor's well-established dominant electric utility.

value.name: DTE Energy
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Ann Arbor's residential solar customers this session; DTE Energy is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

permit_authority.notes: Michigan's Residential Code (currently the 2015 edition — a 2021 IRC update was filed in 2025 but delayed by a court order, per state guidance referenced this session) sets the statewide baseline, but enforcement is delegated to whichever local jurisdiction (city, township, or county) has assumed local-enforcing-agency status; where none has, Michigan's state Bureau of Construction Codes enforces directly. Ann Arbor's own city government administers its expedited residential solar permitting process directly.

interconnection_url.notes: DTE's residential interconnection runs through its Rider 18 Distributed Generation Program. DTE's interconnection process overview says the interconnection process takes approximately six weeks, that DTE emails whether an application is approved or needs changes within 10 business days of receiving the application and fee, and that the installer then uploads the construction documents, including an approved electrical inspection sticker, photos, a photo showing the disconnect switch within 5 feet of the meter, and a signed Parallel Operating Agreement, before DTE's site visit; the installer completes DTE's application in PowerClerk. DTE's Level 1 and 2 procedures list a $50 applicant cost for Level 1, defined as a certified project of 20 kWac or less, under Rider 18. These are the utility's steps and durations, not a City of Ann Arbor permit review time.

battery_programs.notes: The City's own page notes that residential rooftop solar installations WITH battery storage are excluded from the expedited permitting program and follow a different (unspecified, not detailed on the page fetched this session) procedure — this describes a permitting-track distinction, not a financial battery incentive program, which was not independently confirmed this session.

Roof access and ventilation documentation, per the City's own PDF guide
An additional permit for compliance review (including all-black panels/hardware requirements)

required_documents.notes: Per the City's own 'Solar in Ann Arbor' page. Systems with battery storage do not qualify for the expedited process and follow a different, unspecified procedure.

inspection_steps.notes: Not detailed on the City's own page fetched this session.

timeline_days.notes: No City of Ann Arbor permit review time is stated in the sources reviewed. DTE's interconnection process duration is the utility's, and is recorded under the interconnection field, not as a permit timeline.

value.program_or_pathway: Expedited electric-permit-only process (excludes systems with battery storage)
other_conditions: Residential rooftop solar installations WITH battery storage are not eligible for the expedited permitting program
Properties in a historic district require an additional permit, with requirements including all-black panels and hardware
The 20kW figure recorded here reflects DTE's Rider 18 Category 1 threshold (the tier most residential systems fall under), not a separate City permit-eligibility limit

value.name: City solar permit fees (line item solar fees, application fees, plan reviews)
value.unit: waived for approved projects under the expedited process
value.notes: Per the City's own page, verbatim: 'we do not charge for line item solar fees, application fees, or plan reviews' for approved residential solar projects.

value.name: DTE Energy Rider 18 interconnection application fee, Category 1 (systems ≤20kW)
value.notes: Per DTE Energy's Level 1 and 2 interconnection procedures (Rider 18 applicant costs) — this is a utility interconnection fee, separate from the City's $0 permitting fee.

permit_fees.notes: A genuinely notable finding: Ann Arbor charges no city-side fees at all for approved residential solar permits under its expedited process, though DTE's separate utility interconnection fee still applies.

rebates.notes: No specific Ann Arbor or statewide Michigan rebate dollar amount was independently confirmed from a primary source this session — left null rather than guessed.
